verses.1: And behold, a man of God came from Judah with the words of Jehovah. He went into the Temple and stood on the altar to burn incense.
verses.2: And he called out to the priests with the words of God. He said, “Priests! Priests! Hear this: Here comes a son born of the house of David, named Josiah. He will destroy your priests who are corrupt and wicked. And human bodies will be burned upon you.”
verses.3: And on that day, it was said, “This is the judgment that Jehovah has decreed: the altar will be broken down, and the smoke that covered it will be poured out.”
verses.4: And when the king heard what the man of God said regarding the altar in the temple, he sent Joram up to the altar, saying, “Take his hand away from it. His hand has been injured, and he cannot bring it back to its place.”
verses.5: And the altar was torn apart, and the fire spilled from it, just as God’s servant had commanded in Jehovah’s word.
verses.6: And the king said to the man of God, “Please, have mercy on my face before Your God. Pray for me, and restore my hand to me.” And the man of God had mercy on the king’s face. Then the king’s hand was restored to him.
verses.7: And the king spoke to the man of God. He went to him in the house, and he offered him a sacrifice and gave him a gift.
verses.8: And the man of God said to the king, “If you give me half of your house, I will not go with you. I will not eat bread, and I will not drink water in that place.”
verses.9: For so it was commanded to me by the words of the LORD: “Do not eat bread, do not drink water, and do not return along the path you once took.”
verses.10: And he went along another path, and did not return along the path by which he had come to the house of El.
verses.11: And one old man, who lived in the Temple of God, came forward and told him everything that man of God had done that day in the Temple. He also told them what things he had said to the king. They then told their father about it.
verses.12: And their father said to them, “This is the way in which God’s Son walked. And their sons saw the path that God’s Son followed.”
verses.13: And he said to his sons, “Make me a chariot.” They made him a chariot, and he rode on it.
verses.14: And he went after the man of God. He found him sitting under the tree. He said to him, “You are the man of God who came from Judah.” And he replied, “I am.”
verses.15: And he said to him, “Go with me into the vineyard and work there.”
verses.16: And he said, “I cannot return to you, nor can I come to you. I will not eat bread, nor will I wash you with water in this place.”
verses.17: For what I have said to you from the LORD, do not eat bread there, and do not drink water there. Do not go back along the path you used to walk on.
verses.18: And he said to him, “I too am a prophet like you. The Lord spoke to me, saying, ‘Take him back to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water.’”
verses.19: And he sat down, ate bread in his house, and drank water.
verses.20: And they sat down at the table. Then God’s words were spoken to the prophet who had been sent.
verses.21: And he called out to the man of God who came from Judah, saying, “Thus says the LORD: Because you have disobeyed the commands of the LORD your God, and because you have not kept His laws, so this will happen to you.”
verses.22: And she sat down and ate bread, and she drank water in the place where it was said to us: “Do not eat bread, and do not drink water. Do not let your carcass enter the grave of your ancestors.”
verses.23: And after he ate his bread and drank his water, he lost his strength. The prophet was able to revive him.
verses.24: And he went along, and he found him on the road. He killed him. His body was left lying in the road. The lion stood beside the dead body, while the other animals stood beside it as well.
verses.25: And behold, there were men walking by. They saw the donkey being thrown down along the road. There was also a lion standing beside the donkey. They came and spoke to the people living in the city where the old prophet lived.
verses.26: And the prophet heard that man who had been brought back from the road. He said, “This is the man of God; he is the one who opened the mouth of Jehovah. Jehovah gave him to Arah and Arah killed him, as Jehovah commanded.”
verses.27: And he said to his sons, “Carve out a place for me in the midst of them.” And they did so.
verses.28: And he went and found that his prey was lying on the road. The lion stood beside the prey. But the lion did not eat the prey, nor did it break open the carcass.
verses.29: And the prophet lifted up the body of the man of God, laid it on the ground, and placed it in a proper position. Then he went to the city where the old prophet lived, in order to perform the funeral rites and bury him.
verses.30: And he buried his body in the ground, and his brothers laid flowers upon it.
verses.31: And after he died, he said to his sons, “In my death, you must also be buried in the same way that God’s people are buried with their dead. You must place your bodies with mine.”
verses.32: For it shall be that what is spoken by the Lord regarding the altar in the Temple, and regarding all the idols in the cities of Samaria, shall come true.
verses.33: After this event, Yeravam did not return to his evil ways. Instead, he turned around and became a priest of death. He wanted to fill his hands with blood. And so, he became a priest of death.
verses.34: And this became a cause of punishment for the house of Jeroboam, and it led to their destruction and elimination from the face of the earth.
